Subject: Data handling & subprocessors — follow-up from discovery call

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the open items we committed to follow up on: 

- Scope of PII: you flagged customer name, email, account IDs, and payment card tokens as PII that must not be stored unencrypted. Please confirm if transaction metadata (merchant IDs, timestamps) is considered sensitive.
- Retention: you mentioned a 7-year retention requirement for transaction records and 90 days for debug logs. I noted we typically retain detailed request logs for 90 days by default and aggregated telemetry longer.
- Logging controls: need options for redaction/scrubbing of PII from request logs, and an option to disable request-body logging for specific routes.
- Data residency: primary requirement is US-only storage for Maple Financial production data; dev/staging can be multi-region.
- Subprocessors: you asked for our current subprocessor list, specifically telemetry vendors, monitoring, and SaaS marketplace flows (billing exports).

Deliverables we will send by Monday:
- Subprocessor matrix (current) — includes vendor purpose, data types accessed, and region.
- Draft DPA with the residency and retention clauses updated per today’s call (for your legal).
- Short note on logging controls and how to disable request-body logging or apply PII scrubbing rules.

I’m attaching the subprocessor matrix and DPA draft for your initial review. Please flag anything missing and share any vendor-specific questionnaires you want us to complete.

Next steps: propose a 60-minute security deep-dive week of 4/13–4/15 with your security team + our SE + legal. Aditya will send calendar options.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the concise notes — this captures the main points. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- PII scope: confirm that payment card tokens are treated as PCI-derived tokens (we don’t want them stored in readable form outside our PCI boundary).
- Retention: 7 years applies to settlement records only; for request logs we can accept 90 days if we can request on-demand exports prior to deletion.
- Residency: production data must remain in the US. If any subprocessor moves data outside the US, we need prior written consent.
- Subprocessors: please call out telemetry/monitoring vendors (Datadog) and any billing/marketplace flows that push usage to third-party portals.

We’ll review the attachments and circulate any legal redlines. I’ll also share our vendor questionnaire (it’s a short 15-question security attestation) before Monday so you can confirm what’s already covered.

Sara
VP, Product — Maple Financial

Hi team —

I put together a short tech note (summary below) — I’ll attach a one-pager to the internal thread and the customer-facing FAQ we can send: 

- Telemetry & monitoring: we send only aggregate metrics and health pings to Datadog. No raw prompts or model responses are forwarded to external telemetry vendors by default. Trace-level traces for debugging are optional and can be disabled per-customer.
- Request logging: two layers — (1) request metadata (route, timestamp, model, token count) retained for 90 days; (2) request/response bodies are redactable. We support server-side scrubbing hooks that can remove PII before it is written to logs.
- Data residency & storage: production model state and customer data for Maple will be pinned to AWS us-west-2 by default. Backups are encrypted at rest; we can add a contractual clause that backups remain within the US.
- Marketplace/billing flows: if the customer buys via a cloud marketplace (GCP/AWS/Azure), usage reporting may flow to the marketplace billing system. We can provide an option to use direct billing to avoid marketplace usage exports to third parties.

Attachments (internal): redwood-telemetry-note-20260413.pdf, redwood-logging-config-examples.txt

Happy to turn the internal one-pager into a short customer-facing bullet doc for the 4/14 security call.

— Vivek
